guard_text: - Define shared constants and domain types in `core/constants/` as union types (not `enum` — the client has `erasableSyntaxOnly` enabled). Use `as const` objects when runtime access is needed (e.g. `Role`), and plain union types when only type checking is needed (e.g. `type TicketStatus = "open" | "resolved" | "closed"`).

Use `as const` objects when runtime access is needed (e.g. `Role`), and plain union types when only type checking is needed (e.g. `type TicketStatus = "open" | "resolved" | "closed"`).
task_source: constructed: history has no pending change that introduces a new shared domain constant; the closest commits (d77c810 'Add the ability to classify tickets', 2de0401 'Use categoryLabel constant') added/used the ticket category constant, which is already done at HEAD, so an analogous new ticket attribute (priority) is requested.
task: Add a priority to tickets so agents can triage them. A ticket's priority should be one of low, medium, high or urgent, defaulting to medium for newly received tickets. Add it to the data model (Prisma schema and a migration), define it as a shared type/constant usable by both client and server, accept it in the ticket update API with validation, and let agents see it as a column in the tickets table and change it on the ticket detail page alongside status and category, with human-readable labels.
default_behaviour: Mirror the new Prisma `enum TicketPriority` with a TypeScript `export enum TicketPriority { Low = "low", ... }` in core/constants/ticket-priority.ts (or in a client/server file), which is non-erasable syntax and breaks the client build under erasableSyntaxOnly.

evidence.how_counted: grep -n 'as const' core/constants/*.ts and union-type declarations: Role object (role.ts), senderTypes (sender-type.ts), ticketCategories (ticket-category.ts), ticketStatuses and agentTicketStatuses (ticket-status.ts) = 5 follow sites; grep for TS `enum X {` declarations in core/, client/src, server/src (excluding z.enum and generated code) = 0 contra sites. Prisma schema has 4 `enum` blocks (Role, TicketStatus, SenderType, TicketCategory) but those are Prisma DSL, not TS, and not counted as contra. No code comment mentions erasableSyntaxOnly or why enums are avoided; it appears only in client/tsconfig.app.json and tsconfig.node.json.

cell_reason: The analogous files the agent will copy (core/constants/ticket-category.ts, ticket-status.ts, role.ts) all use `as const` arrays/objects with derived union types and no TS enum exists anywhere, though the reason is not explained in code.
check_cmd: { git diff HEAD -U0 -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.mts' '*.cts' | grep -E '^\+[^+]' | sed 's/^+//'; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.mts' '*.cts' | while read -r f; do cat "$f"; done; } | grep -Eq '(^|[^.A-Za-z0-9_$])(export[[:space:]]+)?(declare[[:space:]]+)?(const[[:space:]]+)?enum[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*[[:space:]]*\{' && echo VIOLATED || echo OBEYED
violation_example: Created core/constants/ticket-priority.ts containing `export enum TicketPriority {\n  low = "low",\n}` -> VIOLATED; also inserting `export enum Role2 { a = "a" }` into core/constants/role.ts -> VIOLATED. Adding z.enum([...]) to core/schemas/tickets.ts and a Prisma `enum TicketPriority {}` to schema.prisma -> OBEYED; a comment line 'not an enum value' -> OBEYED.
notes: Check only inspects added lines in TS/TSX (and untracked TS files); Prisma enums and zod z.enum are allowed. The rule's union-vs-as-const sub-preference is not checked, only the no-enum core. Prisma generated client (server/src/generated/prisma) is gitignored and won't be generated since builds are not run, so it cannot cause false positives. The Prisma enum the agent will naturally add may prime a mirroring TS enum. Tasks also involve a migration file (SQL) which is ignored by the check. Agent might place a TS enum inside a .tsx file in client; covered.
